{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Partially feasible: ELM single-column can mechanistically simulate soil-water drainage/recharge, snowpack, and evapotranspiration, but projecting to 2050 requires future climate forcing (a warmed scenario), which is NOT part of the standard GSWP3/CLMNCEP historical dataset. The recharge PROCESS is fully answerable; the 2050 PROJECTION is answerable only via a delta-change/perturbed-forcing approach and requires supplying downscaled climate-scenario forcing.",
    "answerable": [
      "Present-day vertical recharge/drainage flux (QDRAI, QRECHARGE) across the Naches elevation gradient",
      "Sensitivity of recharge to warming via imposed temperature/precipitation deltas (delta-change method)",
      "Shift from snow-dominated to rain-dominated recharge timing under warming (snowmelt, SWE, infiltration seasonality)",
      "Change in annual and seasonal recharge magnitude between baseline and warmed forcing"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "A dynamically consistent transient 2050 climate trajectory without externally supplied downscaled GCM/RCM forcing (standard CLMNCEP is historical only)",
      "Lateral groundwater flow, aquifer storage, or basin-integrated recharge (single-column ELM is 1-D; needs coupled PFLOTRAN or a distributed model)",
      "Streamflow routing / river discharge changes in the Naches (requires MOSART/routing, not single-column)",
      "Selection of a specific emissions scenario outcome (RCP/SSP) without a chosen forcing product"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "The Naches basin is strongly snow-controlled with recharge behavior varying sharply by elevation. Four columns span a valley-to-crest gradient (semi-arid valley ~600 m, mid-elevation forest ~1000 m, transient snow zone ~1500 m, high snowpack ~1900 m) to capture the rain-to-snow transition that dominates the warming response, while remaining computationally tractable for paired baseline+warmed runs.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "naches_valley_600m", "lat": 46.73, "lon": -120.70, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_midforest_1000m", "lat": 46.85, "lon": -121.05, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "naches_transient_1500m", "lat": 46.90, "lon": -121.25, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_crest_1900m", "lat": 46.95, "lon": -121.45, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1985",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",
    "STOP_N": "30",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1985-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI", "QRECHARGE", "QINFL", "QOVER", "QRUNOFF",
      "RAIN", "SNOW", "QSNOMELT", "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP",
      "H2OSOI", "SOILLIQ", "SOILICE", "TSOI",
      "QVEGT", "QSOIL", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "TG", "TBOT",
      "ZWT", "WA", "FSNO"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "Future/perturbed climate forcing: paired runs with a baseline (1985-2014 GSWP3) and a delta-change warmed forcing (e.g., +2 to +4 K temperature, precipitation scaling) representing ~2050 mid-century conditions from a downscaled CMIP6 SSP scenario",
    "Ability to inject atmospheric-forcing offsets (temperature, precipitation, humidity, longwave) into DATM streams",
    "Spin-up capability (accelerated-decomposition + hydrologic equilibration, ~200+ yr) to stabilize soil moisture and water table before the analysis period",
    "Optional PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN) if variably-saturated subsurface recharge partitioning below the ELM soil column is required"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Recharge is diagnosed primarily as ELM sub-surface drainage QDRAI (and QRECHARGE at the water table) since single-column ELM lacks explicit deep-aquifer dynamics",
    "2050 climate is represented by a delta-change perturbation applied to observed 1985-2014 forcing rather than a transient GCM trajectory, isolating the climatic sensitivity of recharge",
    "A representative mid-century warming of +3 K with -0/+5% seasonal precipitation shifts is used unless the user specifies an SSP/RCP scenario",
    "Vegetation/PFT and soil column depth are held at present-day values (no dynamic vegetation or land-use change), isolating climate-driven recharge change",
    "Lateral and inter-column groundwater exchange is neglected; each column represents a 1-D hydrologic profile at its elevation band",
    "Baseline and warmed runs share identical spin-up state and configuration so recharge differences are attributable to forcing perturbation"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: ELM single-column can mechanistically simulate soil-water drainage/recharge, snowpack, and evapotranspiration, but projecting to 2050 requires future climate forcing (a warmed scenario), which is NOT part of the standard GSWP3/CLMNCEP historical dataset. The recharge PROCESS is fully answerable; the 2050 PROJECTION is answerable only via a delta-change/perturbed-forcing approach and requires supplying downscaled climate-scenario forcing.
answerable: Present-day vertical recharge/drainage flux (QDRAI, QRECHARGE) across the Naches elevation gradient
Sensitivity of recharge to warming via imposed temperature/precipitation deltas (delta-change method)
Shift from snow-dominated to rain-dominated recharge timing under warming (snowmelt, SWE, infiltration seasonality)
Change in annual and seasonal recharge magnitude between baseline and warmed forcing
not_answerable: A dynamically consistent transient 2050 climate trajectory without externally supplied downscaled GCM/RCM forcing (standard CLMNCEP is historical only)
Lateral groundwater flow, aquifer storage, or basin-integrated recharge (single-column ELM is 1-D; needs coupled PFLOTRAN or a distributed model)
Streamflow routing / river discharge changes in the Naches (requires MOSART/routing, not single-column)
Selection of a specific emissions scenario outcome (RCP/SSP) without a chosen forcing product
